bio_short: Senior Economist working at the intersection of monetary policy, financial stability, and macroeconomic research.
bio: Senior Economist working at the intersection of monetary policy, financial stability, and macroeconomic research. Currently based in Singapore at AMRO, engaging with policymakers and academia across the region and translating sophisticated economic analysis into sharp policy insights.

Career spanning international organizations, China's central bank, and investment bank CICC, with experience in policy formulation, team management, and international cooperation with the BIS, IMF, and major central banks.
Trained at Tsinghua University, obtaining a B.Sc. in Mathematics and Physics, an M.Econ. in Finance, and a Ph.D. in Economics, with research experience at Princeton and the BIS.
Drawn to the defining questions about how inflation and credit evolve, how monetary transmission works across different financial structures, and what institutions can do to preserve stability.

news.html: Two Selected Issues studies on US dollar liquidity and government deposit fluctuations published in AMRO's Cambodia Annual Consultation Report 2026.
The Strength of the Inflation-Output Link in China (with Mikael Juselius) released as BIS Working Paper No 1353.
Began a visiting scholar appointment at the Bank for International Settlements (2025–2026).
Evolution of Physical Forms of Money and Three Perspectives of Its Definition published in China Finance. Read the essay →
China's Shadow Banking in 2020–2022 published in Humanities and Social Sciences Communications, and presented at the joint HKIMR–IMF–BIS–AMRO conference in Hong Kong.
